thread:
maria-ops: noticing a big spike in unacked PD alerts since ~10:02 UTC. pages are getting queued/delivered with ~10-15m delay. customers are starting to ping support. anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

pagerduty-bot: Incoming webhook delivery failures detected for integration 'redwood-alerts'. 120 failures in last 15m. See: https://status.pagerduty.com/incident/abc123 (auto-notify)

jake-oncall: I'm on call - joining bridge now. confirming: alerts are hitting our alerting plane but PD ack events aren't arriving?

maria-ops: right — our monitoring shows alerts generated at 10:00-10:05, entries in the alerts DB, but PD shows delivery timestamps 10-20m later. some never show as acknowledged even after responders said they saw them.

sarah-sre: quick check: is this only for the PD webhook integration or also for direct phone/sms?

maria-ops: mostly the PD webhooks. our fallthrough phone step (Twilio) still sends sms for high-sev, but it's also slower. very patchy.

jake-oncall: creating incident record in incidents channel and spinning up bridge. joining conf: 10.05am bridge -> dial-in 333-222 (see pinned). I'm going to open a pagerduty support ticket, tagging their engineering.

jake-oncall: ACTIONS: 1) open PD support (doing now) 2) enable secondary routing keys + temp escalation to SMS for Sev1 3) notify support & CS teams 4) track customer impact

maria-ops: @ben-customer-success FYI — we may have delayed paging for affected customers. any inbound customer reports yet?

ben-customer-success: customer-facing support is getting multiple threads. provisioning CS with FAQ lines and advising customers we'll follow up. No escalations to legal yet but customers on Dedicated are asking for ETA. We'll prep an outbound note once we know scope.

kevin-sre: digging into our PD integration logs. seeing 429s from PagerDuty webhook endpoint around 10:01-10:12 UTC. body: 'rate limited - too many requests'. But our overall webhook qps is not that high — looks like PD is throttling on their side.

maria-ops: do we have a secondary fanout we can flip to for routing? I remember an old backup integration that posts to ops-sms.

jake-oncall: yes - two quick mitigations: A) toggle 'fallback-routing' integration to active so alerts also fan out to Twilio/SMS. B) change the PD integration to batched push (reduce webhook rate) OR ramp up retry interval so we don't trigger PD throttling. I'll do A immediately.

sarah-sre: do we have a safe command to requeue alerts to PD once their API recovers? we should avoid duplicates.

maria-ops: we can reemit only alerts with status=unresolved and created_at between 10:00 and 10:15. using this helper:

```bash
# reemit unresolved alerts window to backup integration
./bin/alert-reemit --since 2026-03-15T10:00:00Z --until 2026-03-15T10:15:00Z --target backup-pd-key --dedupe
```

jake-oncall: toggled fallback-routing -> ON. testing with a synthetic Sev1 created now.

ivy-incident-bot: Synthetic alert 'synthetic-sev1-test' created and routed. Delivery to Twilio: SUCCESS. Delivery to PagerDuty: QUEUED (will retry).

jake-oncall: Twilio path looks good. starting controlled reemit of unresolved alerts to SMS only for now. will pause if we see duplicates.

pagerduty-bot: Support ticket PD-987654 opened: "Webhook throttling / delivery delays affecting integration redwood-alerts". Tracker: https://support.pagerduty.com/tickets/PD-987654. Notifying PD on-call.

kevin-sre: PD support confirms they're seeing increased 429s in their ingress cluster and are currently throttling some webhook customers due to upstream load. PD status page shows partial degradation.

maria-ops: estimate impact: about 30% of our high-sev pages delivered >5m late between 10:00-10:20. 2 customers on Dedicated reported delayed incident response. documenting in incident record.

ben-customer-success: started inbound message to affected customers: "We're aware of delayed alert delivery affecting some customers; we've routed critical pages to SMS while PagerDuty resolves their API throttling. We'll follow up with timeline and RCA." :thumbsup:

jake-oncall: coordinating with PD support: asking for ETA and whether they will provide a backlog replay or webhooks will remain rate-limited. Also asked for guidance on safe replays to avoid duplicate incidents.

pagerduty-bot: PD support reply: "We expect mitigation in 30-60m. We're adjusting throttling thresholds and will post update to status page. If you can fan out to a secondary path, that's recommended."

sarah-sre: starting formal timeline notes for postmortem: 10:00 alert surge -> 10:02 PD began returning 429s -> 10:05 we detected queued deliveries -> 10:10 toggled fallback -> 10:18 controlled reemit to SMS -> 10:30 PD reports mitigation in progress.

kevin-sre: small ops detail — when we reemit into PD after they recover, we should set external_id to original alert id so dedupe works on PD side. See code snippet for reemit header:

```json
{
  "external_id": "alert-12345",
  "summary": "<original summary>",
  "severity": "critical"
}
```

maria-ops: good note. jake, want a handoff in 20m? I need to step into a customer call at 10:40.

jake-oncall: yep planning a handoff. @sarah-sre — you'll take over at 10:40 UTC. I'll brief you in 10.

sarah-sre: copy. I'll monitor PD ticket, keep fallback routing active and coordinate replay once PD clears.

ben-customer-success: keeping customers updated. prepping a short incident banner for the console if we confirm > 15m impact to any account.

maria-ops: quick note for post-incident actions: - add circuit-breaker to reduce webhook burst rates - implement exponential backoff with jitter for PD deliveries - verify PD integration supports idempotent external_id field - add synthetic end-to-end alert tests that check PD and SMS delivery paths

jake-oncall: agreed. logging tasks into ops backlog: OPS-459 (circuit breaker), OPS-460 (backoff + jitter), OPS-461 (synthetic tests).

ivy-incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-01. Severity: Sev2 (partial page delivery). Pinned notes added.

pagerduty-bot: PD status updated: "Mitigation in progress; returning to normal within 30-60 minutes." https://status.pagerduty.com/updates/def456

sarah-sre: taking over now. jake — handoff notes?

jake-oncall: Handoff: fallback routing active, synthetic tests green, reemit paused until PD confirms clear (ticket PD-987654). Twilio path handling critical pages. CS notified. Monitoring alert thresholds lowered to catch any missed pages. I'm available on the bridge for 20 more mins.

sarah-sre: thanks — I'll keep the thread updated. once PD fully clears, we'll coordinate a controlled replay with de-dup keys and a follow-up postmortem.

maria-ops: back from call — saw your handoff. one more ask: please include the customer impact matrix in the postmortem (which customers hit Sev1 pages late, timestamps, and any SLA exposures).

ben-customer-success: will compile and attach to the incident doc.

sarah-sre: note for timeline: last observed delayed delivery at ~10:20. PD reported recovery at 10:32 and we observed normal webhook latencies by 10:35. closing bridge but keeping the incident open for RCA.

pagerduty-bot: PD support has posted summary to ticket PD-987654: "Root cause: ingress throttling due to transient upstream overload. Mitigation: rebalanced ingress clusters and adjusted rate limits. Customers advised to implement retry/backoff."

maria-ops: thanks. leaving this open for postmortem. will file RCA draft later today. Good job coordinating the fallback routing quickly. :clap:

sarah-sre: adding action items and owners to the incident doc now.

kevin-sre: small follow-up: let's run an experiment to simulate PD throttling to verify our fallback automation works automatically (OPS-462).

ben-customer-success: prepping customer communications for tomorrow with timeline and actions taken.

ivy-incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-01 status: Monitoring.

maria-ops: closing the incident thread in 4 hours after postmortem posted. If anything else pops up, re-open here. Thanks everyone. :heart:
